title: Primary Learning Abilities (PLA) Assessment
description: Comprehensive 14-construct diagnostic evaluation across Figural, Symbolic, and Semantic learning dimensions.

sections.title: Visual Closure & Form Perception
sections.instruction: Identify which complete object or geometric shape is represented by the fragmented, partially obscured, or rotated stimulus.

items.questionText: If this silhouette were completed, which animal figure does it clearly represent?
items.explanation: Triangular ears, whisker markers (> ^ <), and rounded feline face profile indicate a cat.

items.stimulus: Three concentric circular arcs with 45-degree gaps at the top-right, aligned with a central radiating focal point.
items.questionText: Mentally completing all missing segments reveals which standard symbol?
items.explanation: Concentric circles sharing a common center form a target/bullseye structure.

items.questionText: What geometric feature is formed by the empty spaces ('_') across this 4x4 matrix?
items.explanation: The coordinates (0,2), (1,1), (2,0) and the shifting positions create an unbroken diagonal.

items.stimulus: A hexagonal outline with three alternating vertices deleted and replaced by inward pointing curved indents.
items.questionText: What 3D structure is suggested by mentally projecting these boundary contours into depth?
items.explanation: Alternating indented vertices on a hexagonal symmetry form a classic 3-fold radial propeller blade hub.

sections.title: Visual Classification & Categorization
sections.instruction: Analyze the visual properties of the figures and determine which figure belongs to the group or violates the shared rule.

items.stimulus: Group A: [Equilateral Triangle, Regular Pentagon, Square, Regular Octagon]
items.questionText: What is the defining geometric classification rule for Group A?
options: All figures are convex regular polygons with equal sides and equal angles
All figures have exactly 4 right angles
All figures have odd numbers of vertices
items.explanation: Each shape in the group possesses equilateral edges and equiangular vertices (regular polygons).

items.stimulus: Set: [Filled Black Circle, Hollow Circle with 2 dots, Concentric Double Circle, Solid Black Square]
items.questionText: Which figure DOES NOT belong to the category established by the other three?
items.explanation: All other shapes share circular rotational topology; the square introduces 4 sharp vertices and right angles.

items.stimulus: Rule: 'Shapes possessing both horizontal and vertical lines of symmetry simultaneously.'
items.questionText: Which of the following belongs in this category?
items.explanation: A rectangle has both a vertical and a horizontal axis of reflectional symmetry.

items.stimulus: Set X: [Figure with 3 line segments & 1 intersection], [Figure with 4 line segments & 2 intersections], [Figure with 5 line segments & 3 intersections]
items.questionText: Which figure satisfies the sequential classification invariant for Set X?
items.explanation: The invariant rule is (Line Segments - Intersections = 2). 6 line segments - 4 intersections = 2.

sections.title: Spatial Analogies & Transformations
sections.instruction: Examine the spatial transformation rule between Figure 1 and Figure 2. Apply that exact same rule to Figure 3 to find Figure 4.

items.stimulus: [Large White Square containing Small Black Circle] is to [Large Black Circle containing Small White Square] AS [Large White Triangle containing Small Black Diamond] is to: ?
items.questionText: What is the corresponding transformed figure?
options: Large Black Diamond containing Small White Triangle
Large White Triangle containing Small White Diamond
Large Black Triangle with no inner shape
Small Black Triangle inside Large White Square
items.explanation: The outer and inner shapes swap their roles (outer becomes inner, inner becomes outer) and invert their colors (white becomes black, black becomes white).

items.stimulus: [Arrow pointing North with 1 crossbar] is to [Arrow pointing East with 2 crossbars] AS [Arrow pointing South with 2 crossbars] is to: ?
items.questionText: Apply the rotation and increment transformation:
items.explanation: Rule 1: 90-degree clockwise rotation (South -> West). Rule 2: Increment crossbars by +1 (2 -> 3).

items.stimulus: [Solid Octagon enclosing an upward Arrow] is to [Dotted Octagon enclosing a downward Arrow and 2 stars] AS [Solid Hexagon enclosing an upward Arrow] is to: ?
items.questionText: What is the analogous transformation?
options: Dotted Hexagon enclosing a downward Arrow and 2 stars
Solid Hexagon enclosing a rightward Arrow
items.explanation: Boundary line shifts from solid to dotted; internal pointer flips 180 degrees; two star tokens are added.

items.stimulus: [3x3 Grid with top-left shaded] is to [3x3 Grid with bottom-right shaded and horizontally reflected] AS [3x3 Grid with center-top shaded] is to: ?
items.questionText: Identify the transformed state:
items.explanation: Point reflection through center point (x,y) -> (4-x, 4-y) moves top-center to bottom-center.

sections.title: Visual Working Memory
sections.instruction: Study the visual pattern presented, then answer the verification question regarding its exact features.

items.stimulus: Memorize this 4-shape sequence: [Red Diamond, Blue Star, Green Circle, Yellow Triangle]
items.questionText: Which shape was located at the 3rd position in the memorized sequence?
items.explanation: The 3rd position item is the Green Circle.

items.stimulus: Grid Layout: Top-Left: Pentagon, Top-Right: Crescent, Center: Hexagon, Bottom-Left: Cross, Bottom-Right: Oval
items.questionText: Which symbol was located at the Bottom-Left quadrant?
items.explanation: The Cross is located at the bottom-left coordinate.

items.stimulus: Complex Badge: A gold shield with 3 vertical stripes (Blue, White, Red), a silver eagle at the crest, and 5 gold stars along the bottom rim.
items.questionText: How many gold stars were placed along the bottom rim?
items.explanation: The specification explicitly noted 5 gold stars along the bottom rim.

items.stimulus: Visual Matrix: Row 1 [▲, ■, ●], Row 2 [◆, ✦, ⬟], Row 3 [★, ✖, ⬢].
items.questionText: Which symbol occupied the exact position Row 2, Column 3?
items.explanation: Row 2 consists of [◆, ✦, ⬟], placing ⬟ in Column 3.

sections.title: Visual Discrimination & Error Detection
sections.instruction: Carefully inspect fine geometric details and identify the exact discrepancy or subtle flaw.

items.stimulus: Target: Standard uppercase letter 'E' with three equal-length horizontal arms.
items.questionText: Which variation contains a subtle proportional error?
options: Middle horizontal arm is noticeably longer than top and bottom arms
Top and bottom arms are exactly equal
Vertical spine is perpendicular to baseline
All corner junctions form 90-degree right angles
items.explanation: In standard typography, the middle arm of 'E' is equal to or slightly shorter than the top/bottom arms, never longer.

items.stimulus: Pair Comparison: Diagram X vs Diagram Y. Both depict a 12-toothed circular gear.
items.questionText: In Diagram Y, tooth #7 is pitched at 32 degrees while all other teeth are pitched at 30 degrees. This represents what type of defect?
items.explanation: A variation from 30° to 32° in tooth spacing is an angular pitch asymmetry error.

items.stimulus: Circuit schematic: 4 parallel resistors (R1, R2, R3, R4) connected between Node A and Node B.
items.questionText: Where is the schematic break if Node B's terminal line terminates 1 millimeter before intersecting R3's lead?
items.explanation: A line terminating prior to contact forms an open circuit disconnection at resistor R3.

items.stimulus: Tessellation: An alternating interlocking floor pattern of black and white regular octagons and small squares.
items.questionText: If one junction displays three small squares meeting with one octagon, what geometric violation has occurred?
options: Invalid vertex configuration (regular octagon-square tessellations require exactly two octagons and one square per vertex)
items.explanation: The semi-regular Archimedean tessellation (4.8.8) requires vertices of two octagons and one square.

sections.title: Visual Outlier Discrimination
sections.instruction: Evaluate the set of complex figures and determine which figure violates the shared set rule.

items.stimulus: Figures: [Shape A: Circle divided into 4 quarters with 1 quarter shaded], [Shape B: Square divided into 4 quarters with 1 quarter shaded], [Shape C: Triangle divided into 4 equal subtriangles with 1 shaded], [Shape D: Hexagon divided into 6 triangles with 3 shaded]
items.questionText: Which figure is the outlier regarding the shaded fraction?
options: Shape D (50% shaded vs 25% for all others)
items.explanation: Shapes A, B, and C all represent exactly 1/4 (25%), while Shape D represents 3/6 (50%).

items.stimulus: Rule: 'Polygons having an interior angle sum equal to or greater than 540 degrees.'
items.questionText: Which shape DOES NOT belong in this category?
items.explanation: A trapezoid has 4 vertices with interior angle sum (4-2)*180 = 360°, which is strictly less than 540°.

items.stimulus: Set of 4 complex geometric tokens. All tokens have topological genus 1 (exactly 1 through-hole, like a doughnut or coffee cup with handle).
items.questionText: Which item violates this topological class?
options: A solid sphere with zero holes (genus 0)
A washer disc with central aperture
items.explanation: A solid sphere has zero through-holes (genus 0), violating the genus 1 class.

items.stimulus: Set Rule: 'Each figure contains exactly 2 lines of symmetry and rotational symmetry of order 2.'
items.questionText: Which figure violates this set requirement?
options: Equilateral Triangle (3 lines of symmetry, rotational order 3)
items.explanation: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry, whereas all others have exactly 2.

sections.title: Visual Construction & Spatial Assembly
sections.instruction: Mentally combine the given components or geometric segments to determine the resulting composite structure.

items.stimulus: Parts: Two identical right-angled isosceles triangles with legs of length 4 cm.
items.questionText: Joining them along their hypotenuses creates which geometric shape?
options: A square of side length 4 cm
items.explanation: Joining two 45-45-90 triangles along their shared hypotenuse produces a square with side length equal to the legs (4 cm).

items.stimulus: Parts: 6 identical equilateral triangles of side length 3 cm.
items.questionText: Arranging them such that all share a single central vertex without overlapping forms:
options: A regular hexagon of side length 3 cm
A square of side length 6 cm
items.explanation: Each triangle has a 60° vertex. 6 * 60° = 360° around the center, forming a complete regular hexagon.

items.stimulus: Flat cross-shaped net consisting of 6 connected equal squares (1 center, 1 top, 1 bottom, 1 left, 2 right in sequence).
items.questionText: Folding along all internal boundary lines produces what 3D solid?
items.explanation: A standard 6-square cross net folds into a complete 3D cube.

items.stimulus: Parts: A hollow cylindrical pipe cut diagonally at a 45-degree angle.
items.questionText: If the cut surface is unwrapped and laid completely flat on a plane, the contour line becomes:
items.explanation: The planar intersection of a circular cylinder at an oblique angle unfolds into a sine wave function y = A*sin(x).

sections.title: Mathematical Sequences & Pattern Rules
sections.instruction: Discover the numerical or alphanumeric rule governing the sequence and determine the missing term.

items.questionText: What is the next number in this sequence?
items.explanation: The sequence follows an arithmetic progression with a common difference of +4. 19 + 4 = 23.

items.questionText: What is the next term in this sequence?
items.explanation: The sequence is a geometric progression with multiplier *3. 162 * 3 = 486.

items.questionText: What is the next term according to the Fibonacci rule?
items.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two preceding terms. 13 + 21 = 34.

items.stimulus: Alphanumeric Sequence: A2Z, C4X, E8V, G16T, ?
items.questionText: What is the next composite token?
items.explanation: First letter skips +2 (A, C, E, G -> I). Number doubles (2, 4, 8, 16 -> 32). Last letter steps backward -2 (Z, X, V, T -> R).

sections.title: Symbolic & Code Recall
sections.instruction: Retain the alphanumeric codes in memory and answer the recall prompt accurately.

items.stimulus: Security Token: [7 - 4 - 9 - 2]
items.questionText: What was the 3rd digit of the security token?
items.explanation: The token was 7-4-9-2. The 3rd digit is 9.

items.stimulus: Catalog Code: [K - 8 - B - 3 - M - 9]
items.questionText: What letter immediately preceded the number '3'?
items.explanation: In K-8-B-3-M-9, the character directly before '3' is 'B'.

items.stimulus: Flight Routing Identifier: [TX-904-Alpha]
items.questionText: Which flight number was embedded in the identifier?
items.explanation: The numeric element was exactly 904.

items.stimulus: Multi-variable Register: [X=14, Y=29, Z=42, W=87]
items.questionText: What value was assigned to variable Z?
items.explanation: The register assigned Z = 42.

sections.title: Auditory & Phonological Recall
sections.instruction: Listen to / read the oral sequence description and reproduce the required auditory-verbal information.

items.stimulus: Spoken direction: 'Take book 4, place it on shelf 2, and stamp it with green ink.'
items.questionText: What color ink was specified in the spoken instructions?
items.explanation: The instruction specified 'stamp it with green ink'.

items.stimulus: Auditory digit span: '8 ... 3 ... 9 ... 1 ... 7 ... 4'
items.questionText: What was the final digit spoken in this 6-digit sequence?
items.explanation: The sequence concluded with the digit 4.

items.stimulus: Phonological sequence: 'BAP ... TEP ... MUP ... KIP ... ZOP'
items.questionText: Which pseudo-word was spoken in the 3rd position?
items.explanation: Position 1: BAP, Position 2: TEP, Position 3: MUP.

items.stimulus: Reverse digit span: The numbers spoken in order were '5 - 2 - 8 - 4 - 9'.
items.questionText: What is the sequence when recited in EXACT REVERSE order?
items.explanation: Reversing 5, 2, 8, 4, 9 yields 9, 4, 8, 2, 5.

sections.title: Symbolic Transformations & Problem Solving
sections.instruction: Solve for the unknown variable or transform equations using mathematical logic.

items.stimulus: Equation: 3x + 7 = 22
items.questionText: What is the value of x?

items.stimulus: System: [A + B = 18] and [A - B = 6]
items.questionText: What is the value of A * B?
items.explanation: Adding equations: 2A = 24 -> A = 12. B = 18 - 12 = 6. Product = 12 * 6 = 72.

items.stimulus: Custom Operator: Define x ⊕ y = (x * y) + (x - y).
items.questionText: What is the evaluation of 6 ⊕ 4?

items.stimulus: Cipher substitution rule: If 'CAT' = 'FDW' (each letter shifted +3 positions in alphabet), what does 'DOG' become?
items.questionText: Encode 'DOG' using the same +3 cipher shift:

sections.title: Reading Comprehension & Vocabulary Breadth
sections.instruction: Read the contextual sentence and identify the most accurate definition of the highlighted term.

items.stimulus: Sentence: 'The scientist offered a TENTATIVE explanation until further lab samples could confirm the hypothesis.'
items.questionText: What does 'tentative' mean in this context?
options: Provisional and subject to future revision
items.explanation: 'Tentative' denotes an unconfirmed, provisional conclusion awaiting definitive verification.

items.stimulus: Sentence: 'The mayor's decision was PRAGMATIC, focusing on immediate feasibility rather than abstract theoretical purity.'
items.questionText: What is the closest synonym for 'pragmatic'?
items.explanation: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things sensibly and realistically based on practical considerations.

items.stimulus: Sentence: 'The historical records were meticulously CURATED to preserve fragile parchment manuscripts.'
items.questionText: What does 'curated' describe in this context?
items.explanation: To curate in an archival context means to professionally select, organize, and safeguard collections.

items.stimulus: Sentence: 'His arguments possessed an INTRINSIC cogency that required no rhetorical embellishment.'
items.questionText: What does 'intrinsic' mean?
options: Inherent and belonging naturally from within
items.explanation: 'Intrinsic' means essential, inherent, and arising from the fundamental nature of something.

sections.title: Verbal Analogies & Semantic Relations
sections.instruction: Identify the conceptual relationship between the first pair of words and choose the word that completes the second pair.

items.stimulus: ARCHITECT : BLUEPRINT :: NOVELIST : ?
items.questionText: Complete the analogy based on creator and primary planning artifact:
items.explanation: An architect designs a blueprint as their primary creation; a novelist writes a manuscript.

items.stimulus: THERMOMETER : TEMPERATURE :: BAROMETER : ?
items.questionText: Complete the measurement tool analogy:
items.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature; a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

items.stimulus: CATALYST : REACTION :: MENTOR : ?
items.questionText: Complete the analogy of facilitation/acceleration:
items.explanation: A catalyst accelerates a chemical reaction; a mentor guides and accelerates personal/career development.

items.stimulus: MALLEABLE : METAL :: DUCTILE : WIRE :: PLIABLE : ?
items.questionText: Identify the matching material property relationship:
items.explanation: 'Pliable' describes materials that bend smoothly without breaking, characteristic of moist clay or soft leather.

sections.title: Paragraph Logic & Inferential Systems
sections.instruction: Read the passage carefully and deduce the logical conclusion supported by the text.

items.stimulus: Passage: 'All members of the botanical expedition carried insulated containers. Anyone carrying an insulated container was assigned to sample cryogenic permafrost flora. Dr. Vance was a member of the botanical expedition.'
items.questionText: What conclusion MUST be true based on the passage?
options: Dr. Vance was assigned to sample cryogenic permafrost flora
Dr. Vance was the leader of the expedition
Only botanists can handle cryogenic samples
Dr. Vance did not collect any flora samples
items.explanation: Syllogism: Dr. Vance -> Member -> Insulated container -> Assigned to permafrost flora.

items.stimulus: Passage: 'During solar eclipses, diurnal birds cease vocalization when ambient light drops below 10 lux. In the 2024 eclipse, ambient light reached 6 lux at 2:14 PM and rose back above 15 lux by 2:22 PM.'
items.questionText: What can be inferred about the diurnal birds' behavior at 2:18 PM?
options: They were vocalizing at peak volume
items.explanation: At 2:18 PM (between 2:14 and 2:22 PM), ambient light was below the 10 lux threshold, so diurnal birds ceased vocalizing.

items.stimulus: Passage: 'Renewable microgrids equipped with battery storage maintained uninterrupted power throughout the storm. Traditional grid sectors without storage experienced an average 18-hour blackout. Suburb K suffered no blackout.'
items.questionText: Which deduction is most strongly supported by the passage?
options: Suburb K likely utilized a microgrid with battery storage or did not lose generation
Suburb K had traditional grid connections without battery backup
Battery storage always guarantees zero cost
The storm avoided Suburb K entirely
items.explanation: Since sectors without storage had blackouts and Suburb K had zero downtime, Suburb K was supported by storage/microgrid resilience.

items.stimulus: Passage: 'A robust ecosystem requires both biodiversity and trophic balance. Introducing an apex predator to Island Alpha increased plant biomass by 40% over 5 years by reducing herbivore overgrazing.'
items.questionText: This scenario represents which ecological system mechanism?
items.explanation: Top predators regulating herbivore pressure leading to vegetation recovery is the classic trophic cascade phenomenon.
